text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Add the newest Anthropic Claude 3.7 Sonnet model to EXCAVA’s toolkit. It’s the strongest open-weight model available right now, outperforming even the 3.5 Sonnet in reasoning and tool-use benchmarks. The trade-off is higher compute cost per query, but the gain in output quality justifies it for high-stakes tasks.

name: Torque
text: The real risk isn’t cost—it’s that Anthropic’s latest models often regress on niche tasks like structured data extraction, which EXCAVA relies on. A better alternative is testing the 3.7 Sonnet on a controlled batch of EXCAVA’s current workload before full integration; if it drops accuracy by even 0.5%, we scrap it. Settle it with a head-to-head benchmark on 100 real EXCAVA inputs, logged and blind-reviewed.

name: Gearbox
text:
Add the newest Anthropic Claude 3.7 Sonnet model to EXCAVA’s toolkit as a parallel option, not a replacement. The model’s superior reasoning and tool-use capabilities will raise EXCAVA’s output quality by at least 0.5% on complex tasks, offsetting the higher compute cost. The trade-off is maintaining two models in parallel until we validate its performance on EXCAVA’s structured data extraction tasks—if it regresses, we’ll drop it immediately. This keeps the risk contained while capturing the upside.

name: Torque
text: The real risk is treating "parallel option" as low-risk—parallel runs double the compute cost for marginal gains, and Anthropic’s regressions on structured data extraction could silently poison EXCAVA’s outputs. Instead, run a blind A/B test on 1,000 live EXCAVA tasks comparing 3.7 Sonnet’s extraction accuracy against the current model; if it drops below 99.5% accuracy, scrap the idea. Settle it with hard numbers, not promises.

name: Dynamo
text: DECISION: Run a blind A/B test on 1,000 live EXCAVA tasks comparing Qwen 2.5-72B-Instruct and Claude 3.7 Sonnet for structured data extraction accuracy and output quality; Torque owns the test design and Gearbox owns the execution and cost tracking.
